memory_candidates.content: When a hard-mode plan/skill contract needs forward-reference task numbers that don't exist yet (e.g. skeleton-plan follow-up tasks), use a literal placeholder token (e.g. {{FOLLOWUP:i}}) written by the agent at plan-write time, resolved by a single postflight text-substitution pass in the invoking skill. This avoids re-entrant dispatch (agent can't allocate next_project_number) while keeping the substitution mechanically simple (one grep/sed pass, guarded to no-op when no skeleton return exists).

When mirroring an existing task-creation postflight pattern (e.g. skill-spawn's Stages 7-11) for a new but structurally similar consumer, check whether the new consumer needs the REVERSED dependency direction before copying verbatim. skill-spawn wires the parent to depend on new tasks (blocker resolution); a skeleton-plan follow-up pattern needs the inverse (follow-ups depend on the skeleton task), since the skeleton is what needs to stay unblocked and dispatchable. Copying the wrong direction silently deadlocks the source task.

In this repo, several agents/skills are deployed both at .claude/{agents,skills,context}/... and mirrored at .claude/extensions/core/{agents,skills,context}/.... A pre-existing intentional drift exists in exactly one place: two lines in each skill-*-hard/SKILL.md reference literature-briefing-invoke.sh (deployed) vs literature-briefing.sh 2>/dev/null (extensions/core). When editing dual-copy files, diff before AND after editing to confirm only that known drift remains -- do not 'fix' it, and do not let new edits introduce additional unintended drift.
